Sports.title: Athletes who hate their sports: From a Premier League winner who doesn't watch football to an Ally Pally world champion that isn't a fan of darts
Sports.content:
There are a number of pulls when it comes to a career in sport.

The chance to spend every day doing what you love, earning your living along the way. Or maybe the pursuit of glory, the drive to be the best at what you have dedicated your life to. How about the sometimes staggering prize money on offer, which can lead to the chance of fame and a lifestyle most can only dream of?

Few consider that, for some, it's not really a choice. It's what athletes know – what they have always done, so they will continue to do.

That seems to be the case for three-time darts world champion Michael van Gerwen, who this week spoke about how he's not a fan of darts and doesn't actually follow his sport.

And he's not alone. Some of the top names in tennis, football and more have expressed their dislike and distaste for the games that have given them so much.

Here, Daily Mail Sport takes a look at some of the world's top athletes who aren't actually too fond of the sport they have found success in.

Three-time darts world champion Michael van Gerwen revealed this week that he does not enjoy watching darts

Michael van Gerwen – Darts

Three-time world champion Michael van Gerwen has dropped down to world No 7 after the Matchplay, and his stocks have fallen significantly since his last world title in 2019.

The Dutchman has been speaking about his relationship with darts – the sport in which, perhaps for the first time in a decade, he is no longer the biggest star.

'I never did in my life,' he told Winmau of watching games. 'I don't even like watching darts.'

Luke v Luke (Littler and Humphries) has been the talk of the town for the last couple of years, while Littler has taken his game to a new dimension in recent months in becoming the first darts player to pick up £3million worth of earnings in two years.

Van Gerwen does make an effort to keep tabs on his rivals, but don't expect to see him in the crowd of any events he's not involved in any time soon, or listening to the likes of Wayne Mardle or Dan Dawson analysing the game on the tele.

But he doesn't totally hate the game. Just prefers to play it – which is fair enough, all things considered.

'Sometimes if a friend like Vincent (Van der Voort) used to play or things like that, or if Luke against Luke are playing maybe a final,' Van Gerwen continued on his viewing habits. 'I put on some live scores, but I'm not going to watch it at all.

'I'd rather play than watch. Simple as that. I always say the same, so it would be really weird to change my opinion.'

Ben White – Football

Arsenal defender Ben White has proven to be a bit of a diverse character in football in recent years. It all came to a head in November 2022, when he fell out with England assistant manager Steve Holland – supposedly over his attitude towards the game.

White is not a fan of watching football unless it's to analyse his own performances. Reports also emerged three years ago that White was not watching other analytical videos while with England.

'I watch myself for analytical reasons,' White recently claimed to The Overlap. 'I watch England, maybe, but I'm always busy doing something. I wouldn't just sit down and watch a game.

'I didn't ever watch football when I was younger. I still don't now.'

But, as is the case with Van Gerwen, it's not all hate with White. He just wants to be out there playing.

'I just loved the game,' he continued. 'I was always playing it, never watching.

'So I don't know too much about the older generations, but I know (Patrick) Vieira was a very good player. But I don't know the details.'

Ben White (right) has become known for his dislike of watching football

Serena Williams – Tennis

Serena Williams is perhaps the most famous name in women's tennis history, and one of the most dominant too.

'I don't love tennis today, but I'm here, and I can't live without it,' she told TennisNow in 2012. 'So I'm still here and I don't want to go anywhere any time soon.'

That's despite winning seven Australian Opens, seven Wimbledon titles, six US Opens and three French Opens. But it's not just tennis – it's sport on the whole.

'It's not that I've fallen out of love, I've actually never liked sports, and I never understood how I became an athlete,' she continued. 'I don't like working out, I don't like anything that has to do with working physically.'

Not too much of an issue, though, it seems...

Serena Williams revealed in 2012 that she doesn't love tennis - or sport on the whole

Nick Kyrgios – Tennis

Tennis bad boy Nick Kyrgios has had a bit of a love-hate relationship with his sport.

The Australian, who is planning retirement at the age of 31, reached his first Grand Slam final in 2022 at Wimbledon. He would lose to Novak Djokovic, but has also regularly made headlines for his actions away from the actual tennis, such as his shouting during matches.

One wonders if his relationship with tennis is related to that. He said in 2015: 'I don't really like the sport of tennis that much. I don't love it.'

He does, though, have love for a different sport.

'It was crazy when I was 14,' he continued. 'I was all for basketball and I made the decision to play tennis. I got pushed by my parents and to this day I can still say I don't love the sport. It is just crazy how things go.

'It's good when you're out there on a tennis court. There's nowhere to hide. It's all you, tactically, physically, mentally. But I just love basketball, I love the sport. I always have. I try when I'm on the road with tennis not to watch too many basketball videos and stuff like that, to keep me focused, but it's tough.'

What could have been.

Nick Kygrios has a love-hate relationship with the sport - and would rather have been a basketball player

Mark Williams – Snooker

Things seem to be going a little better for Mark Williams since his comments in 2019, when he became one of the few athletes to actively say they 'hate' their sport.

Currently World No 8 and a 2025 World Championship finalist, the Welshman was going through a tough patch back in 2019 when he had just beaten Fraser Patrick 6-2 in the first round of the UK Snooker Championship.

Despite actually being ranked No 3 in the world, Williams had failed to win a ranking event all year. He lashed out at snooker, and, like Kyrgios, his mind was elsewhere.

'I really struggled but somehow he struggled more than me and made it easy for me on a couple of frames,' Williams said. 'It's going all right, I'm enjoying myself when I'm on the golf course.'

When questioned on snooker, he added: 'Hate it. I'm just enjoying playing golf more.'

He had also talked about retirement in 2017, before going on to become world champion for a third time a year later.

Maybe he feels differently now.

Mark Williams admitted to 'hating' snooker in 2019 after teasing retirement a few years earlier

Tyson Fury – Boxing

Potentially the biggest name in modern boxing doesn't actually like boxing.

Tyson Fury has retired and un-retired countless times, but attributes his many returns to an addiction that helps him deal with his mental health struggles.

'I've tried to walk away many times and been unsuccessful,' he told DAZN in 2024. 'I meant it when I retired after Dillian Whyte back in 2022, I really meant that wholeheartedly. I could have put my hand on the Bible and meant it, but it was difficult to let it go.

'I've been in love with boxing from a little boy. It's been a love-hate relationship. When it's good, it's very good and when it's bad, it's very toxic. Now I am a fully grown adult with a family of my own.

'I wanted to walk away a lot of times but it always drags me back. Boxing is an addiction. It abuses my body, my mind, my soul. But I feel like it takes me to ecstasy. The rush is unbelievable. It gives me the biggest highs ever, but it also gives me the lowest lows. Boxing is more addictive than any drug ever. Ever. You can't let it go.'

It only takes a quick viewing of his reality show to see how much his family have begged him to pack it in. It seems, though, their words aren't enough.

Fury is set to take on Anthony Joshua in an all-British mega-fight later this year, having eased past Mariusz Wach last weekend. After that, he may well retire again – but will seemingly always keep on coming back.

Tyson Fury has tried to retire from boxing a number of times but finds himself returning

Benoit Assou-Ekotto – Football

A pattern emerges in the list of players who don't like their sport. They engage with it in some form all the time – every decision is based on their career, they have to analyse everything about it, and they spend most of their time performing it.

'I play it enough, don't I?' former Tottenham full back Benoit Assou-Ekotto once argued in an interview with Sky Sports.

'I don't watch football. I don't talk about football away from the game either. I suppose that is unusual. My interests are my friends and music, especially hip-hop. I like Ice Cube and 50 Cent.'

Assou-Ekotto played more than 200 times for Spurs, and didn't do too much wrong. Perhaps his argument proves you don't have to be totally obsessed with what you are doing to reach the top level – or maybe it suggests he could have gone higher if he was.

Former Tottenham defender Benoit Assou-Ekotto (right) is another sports star who does not enjoy watching their sport

Andre Agassi wrote in his autobiography that he 'hates' tennis despite his widespread success

Andre Agassi – Tennis

We have saved the most brutal for last – eight-time Grand Slam tennis champion Andre Agassi hates tennis.

'I play tennis for a living even though I hate tennis,' he wrote in his autobiography. 'I hate it with a dark and secret passion and always have.'

Tell us what you really think, Andre.

The American lashed out at the sport in his autobiography, explaining he was forced into it by his father and suffered some painful injuries. Players are also on tour for more than 30 weeks a year, have tennis dominate their lives, and undergo extreme stress.

Agassi won all there was to win. Others on this list have too. Still – it is not always enough. Showing that, sometimes, being a sports star may not be all it can seem to be.

Sports.title: Club at centre of 'Clicky Ponting' scandal hit by fresh 'cheating' claims as umpire releases footage of ANOTHER player seemingly clicking fingers
Sports.content:
A fresh controversy has engulfed the amateur cricket club at the centre of the 'Clicky Ponting' cheating scandal after an umpire released footage appearing to show another player deploying the same tactic.

Saltburn Cricket Club has been at the centre of a storm after fielder Brian Devine allegedly cheated during a Second XI Division Two match against Norton. Video footage of Devine appearing to be clicking his fingers to mimic the sound of a bat edge, tricking the umpire into giving the batsman out, went viral on social media.

On Monday, the North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League launched an investigation into Devine, 38, who has since been suspended by the club for the 'foreseeable future'.

Now, fresh footage has emerged appearing to show another Saltburn player successfully using the same tactic during a Third XI match against Marton.

The fielder appears to click his fingers as the ball flies past the bat and into the wicketkeeper's gloves, prompting the on-field umpire to give the batsman out. The footage was posted on social media by Berkshire-based umpire Andy Smy.

The captain of another team in the same league earlier this week claimed the alleged tactic had not been confined to Saltburn's victory over Norton.

Saltburn have been widely condemned on social media following multiple videos emerging

He said: 'It was not confined to just one game. I was at the other end when one of our players was dismissed and I heard a big sound as the ball went through and immediately thought: "He's out."

'The umpire didn't hesitate either, but our batsman was adamant he was nowhere near the ball and couldn't understand the loud click.

'In all we had three batsmen given out caught behind, but all of them said they hadn't touched the ball. One protested so much the umpire had to speak to him and threaten him with a warning.

'I know of at least three other teams who now have suspicions and it should be noted that in one match against Shildon their wicketkeeper took eight catches.

'You hear of all kinds of things going on in cricket but this is something I haven't heard of before. I hope the league takes appropriate action.'

Earlier this week, Saltburn's Second XI forfeited their match against Marton, dumping themselves out of a cup competition, with a source close to the league saying 'none of the players will have wanted anything to do with this game while they're under such focus'.

They did, however, return to the field on Saturday for a league match against Marton, where table-toppers Saltburn crashed to a nine-wicket defeat. With Devine no longer fielding at slip, Marton chased down their target of 101 in just 20 overs.

Amateur cricket player Brian Devine has been caught appearing to click his fingers to make it appear that a batter has been caught behind when in fact they haven't hit the ball at all

Devine has been dubbed as 'Clicky Ponting' on social media for his alleged actions on the cricket field

Saltburn player has been caught on camera seeming to be clicking his fingers

And Devine, a father and auction mart worker from Guisborough, North Yorkshire, is planning to 'lie low' until the scandal dies down.

A friend said: 'Brian is completely bewildered by the way this has gone all around the world.

'He's had an Australian podcast offering to pay his legal bills today - it's the first he's heard that he's got any legal bills and he's hoping it won't get that far.

'His mates have been telling him to sell his story in Australia, but he just wants it all to go away and hopes he can get back to playing cricket, though at the moment that feels impossible.

'He woke up on Monday morning thinking the world was still the same place he'd left it the night before and suddenly his story was all over the world - in Australia, India, New Zealand and the UK, of course.

'He understands why there is an investigation but the reaction from around the world has knocked him sideways.'

The North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League said it was treating the allegations of cheating 'with the utmost seriousness' and called for the 'rights of all parties' to be respected amid intense scrutiny on social media.

'We would want to place on record our genuine concern for the welfare of those at Saltburn Cricket Club and ask for all to take that into account. There are many people at the club and one of our aims will be to provide them with any wellbeing support we can,' the league said.

'Whilst we understand, to some degree, the interest this issue has generated in the press and media, it is imperative that, now this process is under way, the rights of all parties are observed, including the overriding principles of natural justice and the right to a fair hearing for any individual or entity concerned.

'Anything less risks prejudicing any formal action which may follow.'

Saltburn, in a statement on Wednesday, said: 'This has been a very distressing and stressful experience for all those concerned, and we would ask that this reality is borne in mind and that personal boundaries are respected, as we are an amateur club run entirely by volunteers.'

Sports.title: 'Clicky Ponting' is just the tip of the iceberg. I've played club cricket for decades and these are the wildest stories of cheating, from vaseline to elastic bands and fattening up umpires to a trail of sawdust
Sports.content:
At the snap of a finger, Brian Devine became English cricket's Public Enemy No 1 - and 'Clicky Ponting' was born.

An investigation is underway in the North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League after several videos appeared to show Saltburn CC slip fielder Devine clicking his fingers as the ball passed the batsman to mimic the sound of an edge.

Devine’s aim is as clear as it is shocking – to con the umpire into giving his team a wicket. The spirit of cricket this most definitely is not, and Devine and his team’s actions have shocked the cricketing world (and his now former sponsor, the local curry house).

But Saltburn are hardly the only team over the years to bend the rules – and in some cases, openly break them.

The 2018 scandal which saw three Australian cricketers receive long bans for their part in a sandpaper ball tampering plot and Alex Carey’s controversial 2023 Ashes run out of Jonny Bairstow are high-profile recent examples in international cricket.

And similar incidents to Saltburn’s have taken place regularly at grassroots level, too. We've gathered together the best (or worst, depending on your view) from decades' worth of experience in the glory, and shame, of club cricket.

Brian Devine, the man at the centre of the 'Clicky Ponting' club cricket scandal

Devine (circled) is being investigated by his local league, with allegations he clicked his fingers when the ball passed an opposition player's bat to simulate the sound of an edge

Vaseline assistance

Sunny Agnihotri played for West Blatchington Cricket Club between 2002 and 2008, and won the Sussex Invitation League Division 1 twice.

When they met Crawley Eagles, the opposition would put Vaseline on their bats ahead of the match. The idea was that when the ball nicked the outside edge, it wouldn’t make so much noise.

‘We asked the umpires about it and they said it’s not against the rules,' said Agnihotri. 'They were also definitely rummaging in their pockets between balls, so we knew something untoward was going on. They made it so obvious. The dark arts happen a lot.’

Local rivals Brighton Insurance would waste time when they batted first to use up the daylight.

Between a dismissed batsman walking off and a new one replacing him, you had three minutes. But on the field of play, you could still get padded up. Brighton players would throw all their equipment on the pitch and take longer than three minutes without punishment.

‘They would take double the time so that when it was our turn to bat, it would be gloomier,’ Agnihotri said.

Izzy Martin

But similar incidents to Saltburn’s have taken place regularly at grassroots level too

It’s not always the players…

There was an umpire in the Leicestershire leagues during the late 1990s renowned for getting a twitchy trigger finger the closer it got to opening time at the bar.

When he started to get really thirsty, he would whisper under his breath: ‘Next one that hits the pads… give it a big appeal’ and, when the fielding side did, he duly obliged.

A trick of one former Leicestershire Premier Division champion team was to send beers to the umpires' room and offer them sweets while in the field in a bid to get them on-side so decisions would fall in their favour.

‘Where there’s a will, there’s a way,’ said one member of the side. Their wicketkeeper was also known for trying to kick the stumps down and appealing that the batter had been bowled.

I remember playing in a county age-group match in which one fielder on the team, who went on to become a professional, took a catch on the half-volley and celebrated as though it was clean.

Another team in the Leicestershire leagues was once accused of sending the same batsman in twice in different kit, until their plan was foiled when the star man was spotted by the home team scorer through her binoculars.

Anonymous

No matter the spread of the 'spirit of cricket', the laws are always open to a little bending

Let's all band together

I played in a match many, many years ago where three of our batsmen were given out caught behind, all of them swearing blind they never got a nick on the ball.

After some brief research, we realised the wicketkeeper had an elastic band attached to his glove, which he snapped against it to make the noise of a nick, fooling the umpire into giving it out in a similar trick to Saltburn's.

Anonymous

Saltburn CC, which has now come under international scrutiny after Devine was caught on camera

Questionable declaration

In 2017, Pembrokeshire rivals Carew and Cresselly took on each other in the final game of that year’s West Wales league season. Carew were top, Cresselly second.

Cresselly faced a difficult task that day, but not an impossible one. Carew’s lead was 21 points and a win was worth 20, but then you had the bonuses to consider – a point for every 40 runs up to 200 and a point for every two wickets.

In short, it boiled down to this: if Cresselly could win and take two more bonus points than Carew, they’d snatch the title. But Carew had a devilish plan.

As far as I’ve been told in my retracing of the steps, they even checked the rules with the umpire before the game, found their read of the situation was accurate, and set about putting it in action.

Batting first, they declared on just 18 for one. First there was shock, then revulsion. It was filthy and entirely legal.

Cresselly were welcome to the 20 points, which they achieved by knocking off the chase in just a few overs, but the opportunity for any bonuses had been snatched clean off the table. It was Carew’s title by a single point.

Riath Al-Samarrai

Saltburn weren't the first side to mimick an edge - one of our contributors played against a team whose wicketkeeper used an elastic band!

Bailout

One day, while in action for Saffron Plantationers – a village side in Quendon near Saffron Walden in Essex – I was at the crease with my team needing four runs to win.

My plan was to charge the bowler and hit the ball down the ground. I was still deep in my crease as the bowler ran in. But his delivery was short of a length, so I stepped back and pulled it for four. As I did so, however, I trod gently on my own stumps and off came the bails.

But instead of me being given out hit wicket, as I should have been, everyone at the ground watched the ball disappear to the boundary. Not seeing the bails were off, the umpire signalled four and the end of the game.

After a while, the opposition wicketkeeper noticed something off and questioned why the bails were no longer on the stumps. But I just kept walking off the pitch as technically, the game was now over.

It was one I got away with but I’m not proud of my actions – I got caught up in the moment and should have fessed up. I do seem to remember sleeping OK that night though!

Matt Gatward

Australia captain Steve Smith breaks down at a press conference in light of his side's Sandpapergate ball-tampering scandal in 2018

Another cheat bites the dust

I remember playing for Eynsford at Chislehurst and West Kent one year in the Kent leagues.

Eynsford were interrupted in their victory charge by a short, sharp shower. After 20 minutes off the field to allow the pitch to dry, the umpires suggested a restart and asked Chislehurst to put out some sawdust for the bowlers to allow for better grip.

The response from the Chislehurst captain was: ‘Sorry, we haven’t got any.’

Unfortunately for him, a visiting member had seen him put a bag from the club shed into his car boot, leaving a trail of sawdust between the two locations. When called out, he had the front to say he knew nothing about it!

Anonymous

No age allowances

Not cheating as such, though by way of intimidation it comes close to the line.

I distinctly remember my senior debut in the adult leagues. As someone who had a modicum of talent and was playing Northamptonshire junior cricket at the time, I was chucked in alongside grown men aged just 13 in a bid to speed up my development.

Cricket is meant to be a sport played by gentlemen - but don't be surprised if you hear a few expletives at a village game, no matter how young the person on the receiving end is

Playing for South Northamptonshire village side Marston St Lawrence, I faced a tough task against experienced cricketers. Unsurprisingly given my youth, I struggled with the bat, playing and missing repeatedly.

I was as frustrated as anyone on the field, but my tender years didn’t stop me getting both barrels from the bowler who I couldn’t lay a bat on. I’ll never forget his words.

‘Just hit it, you c***!’ he shouted at me, his words starting off an unpleasant exchange with my more senior partner at the other end.

I was so shocked to be verbally abused at that age, I could not muster a reply. However, in the years since I've thought regularly about what I should have said.

If I had my time again, the response would have been: ‘I’m f***ing trying!’

Alex Bywater

Sports.title: Son of music legend Phil Collins and half-brother of actress Lily Lily joins former Bundesliga champions - but there's a very slim chance he will face Harry Kane
Sports.content:
Phil Collins's son Mathew has signed for former Bundesliga champions 1860 Munich as he continues his football career.

The German side confirmed they have signed Collins, a 21-year-old midfielder on a one-year contract.

Mathew, who was born in Switzerland, had previously been part of the youth set-up at Bundesliga side Hannover 96.

He then moved to WSG Tirol in Austria, before joining second tier side Austria Salzburg last summer.

Collins made four first-team appearances for Austria Salzburg last season, before leaving the club at the end of the campaign.

Phil, 75, had attended one of his matches in November, with Mathew sharing another picture alongside his music legend father in April.

Mathew Collins has signed for former German champions 1860 Munich in the fourth tier

Mathew is the son of music legend Phil Collins, the former drummer and singer of Genesis

Several years ago, rock great Phil opened up on his son's passion for sport.

'Mat loves music, but loves his football even more,' said Phil, the former drummer and later lead singer of rock band Genesis.

'He is certain he'll turn professional. 'The other day he said, "Another five years and I'll be gone."

'He also looks at everything, Bundesliga, French league, everything.'

Mathew's latest challenge with 1860 Munich comes after the historic German side dropped into the fourth tier last season.

1860 Munich had finished eighth in the third-tier 3. Liga last term, but the club were relegated after failing to obtain a licence ahead of the new season.

The club were founding members of the Bundesliga and won the German title in 1966, as well as German Cups in 1942 and 1964.

1860 Munich last featured in the top flight in the 2003-04 season, but have since slipped down the divisions after financial difficulties and the recent failure to receive a licence for the third tier.

Despite being part of the lower leagues, Mathew still could have the chance to face England captain Harry Kane this season should 1860 Munich be drawn against their local rivals Bayern Munich in the German Cup this season.

Mathew had shared a photo with his father after he had watched one of his matches for Austria Salzburg last season

Mathew's half-sister Lily, the star of Emily in Paris, said she 'couldn't be prouder' following his move

Phil isn't Mathew's only superstar relative, with half sister Lily having starred as an actress, most notably in the lead role in Emily in Paris.

Lily showed her support for Mathew's latest move, responding on Instagram: 'Couldn’t be prouder of you! Sooooo exciting!'

Phil revealed this weekend that his children Mathew, Lily, Joely, Simon and Nic had all been summoned to say their final goodbyes to the singer after he almost drank himself to death two years ago.

The 75-year-old singer admitted things could have gone 'terribly wrong' back in April 2024 when he was lying unconscious in a Swiss hospital, prompting his long-term manager to call his five kids to his bedside to make some tough decisions.

Phil told The Sunday Times Magazine: 'Because there were some decisions to be made about 'Do we keep Phil on life support?' kind of thing. My kidneys were packing up, my organs were just seizing up. People were coming to say goodbye...

'But I don't remember them coming, I didn't have no idea this was going on. They were all worried that they wouldn't see me again. It could have gone terribly wrong.'

Phil recovered, though he has a number of other health issues, including type 2 diabetes and nerve damage in his hands, and needs crutches to walk following multiple surgeries on his spine and knees.

Sports.title: Liverpool icon tells Reds what they need to win Premier League title
Sports.content:
Liverpool icon tells Reds what they need to win Premier League title

Liverpool will hope that Andoni Iraola will be able to steady the Reds following a disastrous second season under Arne Slot but former hero Phil Thompson believes a title tilt could be on the cards

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola is set to oversee his first campaign with Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool hero Phil Thompson believes the Reds could be contenders for the Premier League title under Andoni Iraola - but only if they avoid major injuries. The former Bournemouth boss was handed the reins this summer following the decision to sack Arne Slot.

‌



The Dutchman lifted the Premier League crown in his debut season at Anfield but the Merseysiders struggled to hit those heights last term. Liverpool slipped to fifth in the table, just about squeezing into the Champions League.

‌



Since then, they have lost legendary figures Mohamed Salah and Andy Robertson, while Ibrahima Konate quit the club for Real Madrid. Liverpool have invested since then, sealing deals for Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz, while they are chasing a big-money transfer for Paris Saint-Germain star Bradley Barcola.

‌



Giving his verdict on his former side, Thompson believes that another push for the title could be on the cards should Iraola have his star players available throughout the whole season.

"Iraola will need all of his players fully fit, but if we have a fully fit squad, we have a chance of winning the league this year, without question," Thompson told the BBC. “The fans want to see a bit more aggression, but I could see, just from watching (pre-season) from the stands, the demands of the manager.

Liverpool news: Fresh Bradley Barcola transfer boost as improved bid to go in for star READ MORE :

Yan Diomande transfer twist as surprise update emerges on Real Madrid target READ MORE :

"Andoni wants the ball to go forward and that's what we want to see. Go forward, quicker, more precise."

‌



And while a lack of injuries might push Liverpool up the table, Thompson also believes that having vocal leaders in the dressing room might also be a useful asset under their new boss.

"When you have a difficult time — a difficult couple of games or something — you need some strong voices in there, and you just feel like there is only Virgil van Dijk and Alisson Becker who remain at the club," Thompson added.

"I know people go, 'Oh, Dominik Szoboszlai'. But he has only been there a couple of years. He has to step up and I think he will do.

‌



View 2 Images Phil Thompson has shared his thoughts on Liverpool ahead of the new season (Image: Getty Images)

"But there are others around the team who you look to who will have to step up, to lay down some player rules."

Liverpool have just three more pre-season friendlies to navigate against Leeds, Monaco and Como before they kick off their 2026/27 Premier League campaign. The Reds get themselves underway against Newcastle United away from home, before their first match at Anfield against Nottingham Forest.

Sports.title: Man United icon Casemiro's Inter Miami career off to embarrassing start after nightmare home debut
Sports.content:
Man United icon Casemiro's Inter Miami career off to embarrassing start after nightmare home debut

Former Manchester United midfielder Casemiro endured a nightmare home debut for Inter Miami

View 2 Images Former Man Utd midfielder Casemiro had a debut to forget for Inter Miami. (Image: (Photo by Rich Storry/Getty Images))

Former Manchester United midfielder Casemiro had a home debut to forget new club Inter Miami. The Brazilian scored an own goal in the 34th minute as Inter Miami drew with the Columbus Crew.

‌



The 34 year-old played a wayward pass to the opposition, diverting the ball past his own keeper as he tried to make amends by intercepting a cross. His blunder drew the Columbus Crew level after Luis Suarez's opener in the 16th minute.

‌



Casemiro was visibly frustrated by his mistake, but Inter Miami regained the advantage before the break. Noah Allen found the net in the fifth minute of first-half added time to put the home side back in front.

‌



Man Utd handed £42m transfer blow after Michael Carrick made feelings clear READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Brais Mendez scored in the 84th minute to ensure a share of the spoils with a late equaliser. Despite his blunder, Casemiro played the full 90 minutes for the second consecutive match.

His first start delivered a 1-0 victory over Montreal that was marred by a serious injury sustained by his new team-mate German Berterame.

‌



The former Real Madrid star departed Manchester United at the end of the campaign, when his contract expired. The Brazil international enjoyed an impressive final season with United but revealed his intentions to move on at the start of the year.

The experienced midfielder represented his country at the World Cup before his new club was announced following Brazil's last-16 elimination. Casemiro penned a one-year contract, with an option to prolong his stint until 2029.

View 2 Images Casemiro scored an own goal in Inter Miami's draw with Columbus Crew. (Image: (Photo by Leonardo Fernandez/Getty Images))

‌



Speaking earlier in the week, Casemiro disclosed he'd fantasised about lining up alongside MLS sensation Lionel Messi. The World Cup runner-up entered the fray from the substitutes' bench against Columbus to realise his former adversary's ambition.

"The amount of trouble Messi gave me. of course, I dreamed of playing with him," Casemiro said. "I always wanted to play with the best. I could never stop him, I always needed the help of my teammates.

"I am very happy to be alongside him now and I want to continue winning titles with him. I want to enjoy being alongside him, help him and make him even greater. He is one of the gods of football, if not the God of football himself, and I want to help."

‌



Casemiro's switch has arrived with its own share of controversy, though. The MLS confirmed they were examining his transfer after Inter Miami struck an agreement with LA Galaxy for the rights to secure his signature.

"The league is gathering all relevant information and will refrain from further comment until the review is complete," the MLS said.

"While Inter Miami CF and the LA Galaxy have reached a settlement for the discovery priority [first rights] to sign Casemiro, the terms will be released upon conclusion of the tampering investigation."

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino 'certain to go' according to FIFA insiders after botched World Cup plot
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino 'certain to go' according to FIFA insiders after botched World Cup plot

A source described the FIFA President as a 'dead duck' while opponents were reportedly lining up candidates as his successor

Donald Trump addresses his call to Infantino over Balogun

Gianni Infantino looks certain to be ousted as FIFA President after his 'shabby' attempts to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors.

‌



Infantino, 56, could have profited from the "Fifa Forward Enterprise" scheme (FFE) and is trying to stay in his post. But his support is flooding away.

‌



A source told the Sunday Times that Infantino is a 'dead duck' while opponents were reportedly lining up candidates as his successor.

‌



The FA and UEFA, European football's governing body, said that they had lost confidence in Infantino.

In a stinging statement, which the English FA said it supported, Uefa described the scheme as a "shabby, back-room, opaque deal he [Infantino] hatched and tried to force through".

Gianni Infantino sent overwhelming FIFA quit verdict as 99% call for him to go READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino planned to bank £22million salary PLUS bonuses before FIFA ploy collapsed READ MORE :

View 3 Images And it's goodbye from him: Sources suggest Infantino's days at FIFA are numbered (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

‌



It added: "The current Fifa leadership has not only lost Uefa's confidence but also that of many other members of the football family."

Former FA chief Mark Pallios was among those calling on Infantino to go. He said: "He should not survive.

"He has delivered these plans with a complete lack of transparency." England legend Peter Reid slammed Infantino and called for him to resign for the good of the game.

‌



He told the Mirror: "He must go - look at the World Cup: the hydration breaks for advertising, the half time show in the final.

"FIFA has hundreds of millions already, they should be putting more money into grassroots."

CONCACAF, which governs the north and central American associations, plus the Caribbean, called for a "comprehensive reckoning" with Infantino's presidency.

‌



View 3 Images FIFA President Gianni Infantino speaks during the 2026 World Cup draw (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

"A proposal of this magnitude does not reach that stage by accident," CONCACAF said in a statement. "It is a symptom of leadership that has stopped putting football first.

"This recent unilateral and egregious act of poor governance and leadership follows a pattern of missteps and similar behaviour."

‌



Uefa led the way in opposing the plan with its 55 members, including the FA, agreeing on Thursday to boycott all Fifa competitions.

"We cannot keep going on like this with secret schemes on fast-track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game," it said.

"We must identify those responsible and hold them to account. This is a victory for the whole game. But it must not be the end of the story.

‌



"The proposal has gone. The task of rebuilding trust in Fifa has only just begun."

Sources told the Sunday Times that senior figures in FIFA were looking to find a successor to Infantino.

View 3 Images Peter Reid the England legend called for Infantino to resign (Image: Gareth Fuller/PA Wire)

‌



A spokeswoman for the FA said: "We fully support UEFA's position. It is time for a full and robust review of FIFA's leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently, for the benefit of all 211 member nations and with the long-term stewardship of football at its heart."

Infantino is likely to face an emergency FIFA council meeting where he will be asked to resign.

If he refuses, a single candidate backed by all his opponents would be put up to challenge him in next year's election.

Article continues below

Candidates for the role include Concacaf president Victor Montagliani, Asian football president Sheikh Salman and Paris Saint-Germain president Nasser Al Khelaifi.

There may also be support for a less high-profile candidate who has backing from across the various continents.

Sports.title: Josh Kerr jokes 'pressure is for tyres' as he celebrates Commonwealth Games gold medal in Glasgow
Sports.content:
Josh Kerr jokes 'pressure is for tyres' as he celebrates Commonwealth Games gold medal in Glasgow

The world record holder relaxed after he won the One Mile race in three minutes 54.12 seconds, ahead of rising Australian star Cameron Myers, who took silver, while Kenya’s Timothy Cheruiyot won bronze

View 3 Images Josh Kerr with his Commonwealth Gold one mile medal (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

Josh Kerr joked that 'pressure is for tyres' today as he celebrated a turbo-charged Commonwealth gold in front of his home crowd in Glasgow.

‌



The world record holder won the One Mile race in three minutes 54.12 seconds, ahead of rising Australian star Cameron Myers, who took silver, while Kenya’s Timothy Cheruiyot won bronze. The field also included fellow Scot Jake Wightman, who finished fifth.

‌



Kerr, 28, explained that he trained in the stadium as a teenager, learning how to 'win and lose'. Kerr joked that he did not feel the pressure after his world record mile two weeks ago adding: "Pressure is for tyres."

‌



View 3 Images Josh Kerr wins Commonwealth Gold in front of his home crowd (Image: Getty Images)

Gianni Infantino planned to bank £22million salary PLUS bonuses before FIFA ploy collapsed READ MORE :

On being named as 'King of Scotland,' he added: "Stop it. It was incredible, the fans packed the stadium and I knew that I had to seize the moment. I learned my craft there in Scotstoun stadium, it is where I learned how to win and lose. Winning in front of the home crowd was just incredibly special."

He thanked his childhood coach and said: "I am very, very proud to be an Eric Fisher athlete." Kerr said that he hoped to set an example for young athletes. Eric, who is still coaching in Glasgow, said he was very proud to guide both Kerr and Wightman when they were teenagers.

‌



A raucous home crowd roared with delight as Kerr took the lead in the final lap and crossed the finish line comfortably ahead of his rivals. The First Minister presented the athletes with their medals at a ceremony later in the evening.

View 3 Images Josh Kerr after his Commonwealth Gold (Image: Martin Rickett/PA Wire)

Mr Swinney described Scotland’s performance in the Games as “truly historic and inspiring”. He said: “We’ve enjoyed some truly historic performances from Team Scotland at the Commonwealth Games – in swimming, bowls, athletics to name a few.

‌



“I hope that the Glasgow Games will encourage future generations to continue and build on this legacy of sporting greatness.”

The 11-day sporting extravaganza will end with tonight's closing ceremony at the Ovo Hydro. The slimmed down version of the Commonwealth Games has saved the British taxpayer around £600m - and may have secured the future of the event.

The total public funding allocated to stage the Birmingham 2022 Commonwealth Games was £778 million. Birmingham City Council and local partners contributed £184m (25%) of that total.

Article continues below

The remaining 75% (£594m) was covered by the UK central government. Organisers of Glasgow 2026 say that using hotels instead of a village, along with smaller arenas and fewer events, cut costs to around £160m. Victoria in Australia was due to host the event and paid £199m to pull out which has funded Glasgow 2026 without taxpayers paying a penny.

Phil Batty, the chief executive of Glasgow 2026, said: “This definitely isn’t the last hurrah for the Commonwealth Games. What we’ve seen is a wholesale shift in what the Commonwealth Games needs to do to sustain itself, not just through 2030, but through 2034, 2038 and beyond."

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino sent overwhelming FIFA quit verdict as 99% call for him to go
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino sent overwhelming FIFA quit verdict as 99% call for him to go

Gianni Infantino has been told to leave FIFA following the doomed plan to sell off the World Cup with UEFA and CONCACAF declaring losses of confidence in the current president

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino has u-turned on the plan to sell a share in the World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

Gianni Infantino has been told to RESIGN from FIFA by a whopping 99% of Mirror readers. The president finds himself under huge pressure, having performed a dramatic u-turn on his plan to sell off a share of the World Cup to an investment group.

‌



FIFA announced the plot earlier this week, to widespread criticism from fans, governing bodies and even UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham. There were suggestions that some confederations would consider boycotting any FIFA-organised competitions in the face of the plan.

‌



But Infantino and FIFA performed a huge backtrack by cancelling the proposal in its entirety. That, however, has not seen the current president escape criticism, with some still calling for the 56-year-old to be removed from his position.

‌



Since the baffling plan was originally unveiled, Mirror Football has been running a poll for fans to decide whether Infantino should resign or not. In total, 6832 fans had their say, with a huge 99 percent of them suggesting that Infantino’s position was now untenable.

That vote follows UEFA declaring a loss of confidence in the current president. A statement from UEFA on Saturday: "We cannot keep going on like this with secret schemes on fast track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game. We must identify those responsible and hold them to account.

Gianni Infantino planned to bank £22million salary PLUS bonuses before FIFA ploy collapsed READ MORE :

"It is right that, in the coming days and weeks, UEFA will work with its associations and in close cooperation with other confederations to reflect on how this happened and devise a plan to make sure that it cannot occur again. That review should be thorough and fundamental. No option should be off the table. The current FIFA leadership has not only lost UEFA's confidence but also that of many other members of the football family.

‌



"When Gianni Infantino asked for the trust and the votes of FIFA's Member Associations to elect him as their President in 2016, he said, 'Of course we have to be transparent. I have been this in the last 15 years of my life in UEFA.

“You will have to play a part every day in the life of FIFA,' before telling the assembled stakeholders, 'The money of FIFA is your money. It's not the money of the FIFA President. It's your money. You are the national associations and the money of FIFA has to serve for the development of football and not for anything else.'

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino has been told to leave his post (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"On both these promises, he has failed to deliver. The shabby, back room, opaque deal he hatched and tried to force through were anything but transparent."

CONCACAF followed suit with their own scathing statement, while bizarrely the Qatari FA have spoken out in support of Infantino.

A statement read: “We welcome FIFA President Gianni Infantino's decision to withdraw the FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal in the interest of the global football community.

Article continues below

“While the proposal had merit, we applaud the wisdom behind prioritising unity among Member Associations. The Qatar Football Association fully supports President Infantino's efforts to continue growing and strengthening the game globally.”

Sports.title: Ex-Man City captain gives health update after being diagnosed with devastating rare condition
Sports.content:
Ex-Man City captain gives health update after being diagnosed with devastating rare condition

Former Manchester City captain Andy Morrison was diagnosed with neurological condition Ramsay Hunt Syndrome earlier this year but he now appears to be firmly on the mend

View 2 Images Andy Morrison previously captained Man City (Image: Getty Images)

Ex-Man City captain Andy Morrison has revealed how he has left doctors ‘amazed’ with his recovery from Ramsay Hunt Syndrome. The 55-year-old was diagnosed with the devastating neurological condition earlier this year.

‌



The condition is caused by a virus in the facial nerve and can lead to face paralysis, blistering rashes near the ear, severe earache and hearing loss. But it appears that the former City man is firmly on the mend, having issued an update to supporters on social media following a return to the commentary booth.

‌



He said: “Evening everyone. Just a quick update after the first day back working at City with the matchday live team, which I thoroughly enjoyed.

‌



“It was fantastic to be back. Felt the voice was strong enough to go back and do co-commentary today. That's my first time back in five-and-a-half months. I really appreciate all the support and working with Ali Mann, who makes it very easy.

Arsenal star refused to go on pre-season tour to force through summer transfer READ MORE :

“An enjoyable game. I struggled with a few words, a few names, but nothing too bad. I did struggle with (Ryan) McAidoo. Could have a player there by the way, watch this space. There was enough there to think he could be the next one on the conveyor belt, hugely impressive in the second-half.

‌



“Birthday yesterday, that was a great day with grandkids and family. I had a specialist on Wednesday and it was really positive, he was really delighted and amazed at the progress I had made, from House-Brackmann (nerve grading scale) six to a four and he is really positive that within a year I'll get my eye back and be able to blink, so I won't have to tape it down at night.

“I still have to take juice to swallow and I have no taste in the side of my mouth and the whole side of the face is numb, so I have to drink through a straw still. He wasn't sure just how much that would progress because it's still really weak. But if sucking through a straw is worst case scenario then so be it. I won't be posting now because I won't see a specialist for another three months.

View 2 Images Andy Morrison has offered an update on his condition (Image: @AndyMorri5on/X)

Article continues below

“A really good day and it just felt great to be back doing something when that seemed a million miles away. I didn't get out of bed for four weeks and couldn't speak for a month.

"I had some really dark days in this conservatory but I stayed positive and this too shall pass, everything passes, good or bad, everything comes and goes and sometimes you just have to dig in and get through it. But thanks for listening and see you all soon.”

Sports.title: Man Utd handed £42m transfer blow after Michael Carrick made feelings clear
Sports.content:
Man Utd handed £42m transfer blow after Michael Carrick made feelings clear

Manchester United have already been busy in the transfer market under Michael Carrick and some exits could be on the cards before the end of the window but one deal is already under threat

View 2 Images Michael Carrick has some decisions to make in the transfer market (Image: Getty Images)

Joshua Zirkzee might just have seen his Manchester United exit route blocked, with Juventus pursuing alternative targets. The Dutchman was expected to leave Old Trafford this summer following a disappointing couple of seasons.

‌



Zirkzee, 25, joined the club from Bologna for a fee of £36.5m in 2024 but he has gone on to score just nine goals since then - just five of those coming in the Premier League. It was previously suggested that United were happy to cut their losses on him this summer.

‌



A return to Serie A was touted for the former Bayern Munich man, with Juventus emerging as potential suitors. But a switch to Turin now looks unlikely given Juventus’ own business.

‌



According to reports in Italy, the Old Lady are closing in on a permanent deal for French striker Randal Kolo Muani for a fee of around £42m (€50m), while they have also completed a move for Bayer Leverkusen’s Kerim Alajbegovic.

Amad and Leny Yoro in total agreement after JJ Gabriel makes Man Utd debut READ MORE :

Given those two moves, it appears unlikely that Juventus will want to sign Zirkzee as well. The only route to a move to Turin appears to be a swap deal involving the Dutch forward and Francisco Conceição, albeit it remains to be seen whether that is an avenue that the Red Devils want to explore.

He does also appear to have other interest, specifically from Ajax and Premier League sides, but whether that becomes a tangible move, is another matter. It could leave Zirkzee in a very tricky spot, with Carrick appearing to signal that the forward has little future at Old Trafford, having only given him a brief cameo in the pre-season win against Atletico Madrid.

‌



Fellow forward Bryan Mbeumo instead started centrally and enjoyed a productive evening by scoring twice. Speaking about his role, the Cameroonian said: “Obviously, I’m lucky to be able to play a different position and I try to give my best. It depends on the games (where I play).

View 2 Images Zirkzee was only handed a brief cameo vs Atletico Madrid (Image: Getty Images)

“We try to get ready for the first game of the season and we work really hard on the training so it’s really important to have good results as well.

Article continues below

He added: “Obviously I’m always really challenging myself every time and will never regret having this challenge.”

Away from Zirkzee and Mbeumo, United could potentially be left with a decision to make over Benjamin Sesko. According to reports in Germany, Bayern Munich remain interested in the former RB Leipzig man, albeit their focus for now remains on agreeing a new deal with star forward Harry Kane.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
